title: The Locked Wine Cellar
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officers Chiba/Takagi) omitted by convention. case_type: murder. Discrepancies vs. the old wiki-derived case file (cases/ep235_the_locked_wine_cellar.json): (1) the old file's clue c2 states Nonaka 'relocked the door with the victim's own key' referring to the wine cellar door -- per transcript the wine cellar door has an automatic electronic lock with no spare keys and was never manually relocked with a key at all; the key Nonaka stole from Kusaka's pocket was used to relock the BACK DOOR of the house (his own separate escape/alibi route from the backyard), not the cellar. (2) the old file's clue c1 implies the wine-soaked handkerchief was already 'found on him' -- in the actual confrontation Conan never recovers the handkerchief on-screen; he deduces Nonaka must still be carrying it (since discarding a monogrammed gift would itself be suspicious) and demands he produce it, which triggers Nonaka's confession rather than the handkerchief being pre-existing physical evidence in hand. (3) the old file omits Toshiko Kusaka (the victim's wife, who discovers the body with Kogoro and supplies the alibi-narrowing fact that reaching the wine cellar from the kitchen requires passing through the living room) and omits the fingerprint sub-clue (Tonomura's and Takano's prints on the cellar door, Nonaka's conspicuously absent) that Conan uses to eliminate the two red herrings before naming Nonaka. Murderer identity (Takeo Nonaka) itself is confirmed correct by the transcript.

attrs.alibi: went to the wine cellar door to ask Kusaka for more money but did not go inside

attrs.alibi: went to the wine cellar door to ask for an extension on her repayment deadline but did not go inside

locations.name: Living room of the Kusaka household

attrs.note: only through-route between the kitchen and the wine cellar

attrs.trick: threaded through the victim's belt to secure the body, pushed through the wine cellar window, then tilted to lower the body into place between the shelves without the killer ever entering the room

attrs.origin: gift from Toshiko Kusaka, monogrammed with Nonaka's own initials
attrs.use: used to wipe wine off the clothesline poles after the victim's feet knocked bottles off a shelf during the lowering
attrs.status: not recovered at the scene; Conan deduces Nonaka must still be carrying it because discarding a monogrammed gift would itself look suspicious -- confronting him with this demand triggers his confession

attrs.use: lassoed around the window's inside hook from outside and pulled to swing the window shut and re-latch it after the body was placed inside

objects.name: Smashed wine bottles on the cellar floor

attrs.staging_flaw: bottles only fell from the single low shelf the body's feet caught while being lowered through the window; nothing else in the cramped cellar was disturbed, which is inconsistent with a real struggle between two people
attrs.initial_misreading: police first assumed the breakage was from a physical fight between Kusaka and his killer

clues.desc: Fingerprint comparison on the wine cellar door: Tonomura's and Takano's prints are present (matching their own admissions that they approached the door to ask Kusaka for money but never went in), while Nonaka's are conspicuously absent -- not because he was never near the crime, but because his method (clothesline poles through the window) never required him to touch the door at all, which both clears the two red herrings and points to a killer who accessed the room a different way.

edges.method: strangulation with a rope, in the backyard, away from the wine cellar
